article.background: 欧洲媒体与制度文化议题。正式、成熟、清晰，强调欧洲整合、多样性与共同身份，不做戏剧化朗读。

sentences.en: Television is one of the means by which these feelings are created and conveyed — and perhaps never before has it served so much to connect different peoples and nations as in the recent events in Europe.
sentences.zh: 电视是形成并传递这些感受的手段之一；而在欧洲最近发生的一系列事件中，它把不同民族和国家联系起来的作用，或许比以往任何时候都更加突出。

sentences.en: In Europe, as elsewhere, multi-media groups have been increasingly successful: groups which bring together television, radio, newspapers, magazines and publishing houses that work in relation to one another.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲以及世界其他地区，多媒体集团正日益获得成功；这类集团把电视、广播、报纸、杂志和出版社汇集在一起，使它们彼此协同运作。

sentences.en: This alone demonstrates that the television business is not an easy world to survive in, a fact underlined by statistics that show that out of eighty European television networks, no less than 50% took a loss in 1989.
sentences.zh: 仅此一点就足以说明，电视业并不是一个容易生存的领域；统计数据更印证了这一事实：欧洲八十家电视网中，1989年竟有不少于一半出现亏损。

sentences.en: Creating a “European identity” that respects the different cultures and traditions which go to make up the connecting fabric of the Old Continent is no easy task and demands a strategic choice — that of producing programs in Europe for Europe.
sentences.zh: 要塑造一种既尊重构成旧大陆共同纽带的不同文化和传统、又具有整体性的“欧洲认同”，绝非易事；这要求作出一种战略选择——在欧洲制作面向欧洲的节目。

sentences.en: In dealing with a challenge on such a scale, it is no exaggeration to say, “United we stand, divided we fall” — and if I had to choose a slogan it would be “Unity in our diversity.”
sentences.zh: 面对如此规模的挑战，说“合则立，分则败”并不夸张；如果非要选一句口号，我会选择“多样性中的统一”。
